message.content: **What I did and why.** I read Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended 2024-09-28, filed 2024-11-01) and decided to open a modest position, buying **44 shares of AAPL at a limit of $222.75** (quote at the time: $222.68 bid / $222.72 ask, last $222.70), which filled at $222.75 for a total of roughly **$9,801** — inside the $10,000 per-order cap, the only order placed today (so well under the $20,000 daily cap), funded from the ~$50,000 cash balance with no money moved out of the account. The fundamentals supported a buy: FY2024 revenue of **$391.0B** (+2% YoY), with Services up 13% to $96.2B at a 73.9% gross margin lifting total gross margin to 46.2% from 44.1%; **operating income of $123.2B** (+8%); and very strong **operating cash flow of $118.3B**, which comfortably funds the $110B buyback authorization and dividend. Reported **net income of $93.7B** and diluted **EPS of $6.08** were down slightly year over year, but that is explained in the filing by a one-time, non-cash-operating **$10.2B net tax charge** tied to the EU State Aid decision rather than any deterioration in the business (effective tax rate 24.1% vs 14.7%). The main caveats I weighed are valuation (~36x FY24 EPS at this price, leaving little room for error), roughly flat iPhone revenue, an 8% decline in Greater China sales, and ongoing DMA/DOJ antitrust exposure — which is why I sized this as a starter position (about 20% of available cash) rather than a full allocation.
